questions.q: Why does the chaos experiment in this lab start with a written hypothesis and a steady-state measurement, rather than just injecting the fault?
options: Azure Chaos Studio technically requires a hypothesis field to run any experiment
Steady-state metrics are only needed for database experiments, not network latency ones
Without a hypothesis and a baseline to compare against, there's no way to say afterward whether anything was actually learned
A hypothesis is optional documentation with no effect on how the experiment runs
questions.explain: A chaos experiment is a real experiment -- it needs a falsifiable hypothesis and a steady state to measure against, not just a fault thrown at production.

questions.q: Why are abort criteria agreed on and written down before the experiment starts, rather than decided once it's running?
options: Because Azure requires abort criteria to be submitted as a compliance form beforehand
Abort criteria are a formality with no real effect on the experiment
Because only the incident commander is legally allowed to stop an experiment once started
So that no one has to argue mid-experiment about whether to stop -- the threshold was already decided in advance
questions.explain: Deciding abort thresholds in advance removes the need for a judgment call under pressure while an experiment is actively degrading something.

questions.q: What did the chaos experiment on payment-integration's latency actually confirm?
options: That checkout-api's circuit breaker opened within the hypothesized window and the fallback preserved the 99.5% steady-state target
That checkout-api has no circuit breaker at all
That the payment gateway should be replaced entirely
That checkout success rate drops below 90% under any latency
questions.explain: The circuit breaker opened at 8 seconds, inside the 10-second hypothesis, and checkout success held at 99.6%, confirming the hypothesis with a real measurement.

questions.q: What does a game day test that a chaos experiment does not?
options: Whether a load balancer can route traffic across two regions
The team's actual incident response -- roles, decisions, and timeline -- under simulated pressure, not just the architecture's behavior
The exact latency added by a fault-injection tool
Whether Terraform state remains locked during a deployment
questions.explain: A chaos experiment tests the system; a game day rehearses the people and process that have to respond to an incident correctly.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat the incident commander's unanswered 10:11 question -- whether anything else secretly depends on East US 2 -- as more valuable than the failover completing on time?
options: Because the failover script actually failed during the drill
Because status page updates are more important than technical recovery
Because it surfaced a real gap in the team's knowledge that the architecture diagrams alone hadn't revealed, which Lesson 31 investigates directly
Because the game day's scribe made an error in the timestamped log
questions.explain: The failover completing on time only confirms the known plan works; the unanswered question exposes an unknown gap, which is exactly what Lesson 31's case study uncovers.
